messages.author: 3d643362f888e7df
messages.subject: comparing intervention models
parts:
hi

I have a clinically relevant model where a model can reproduce a
pathology. There are a variety of interventions possible which can be
incorporated into the model.

I'd like to do (what I think is) a model comparison of different
interventions, but to identify relative likelihood that the intervention
(modified model) does *not* reproduce a specific aspect of the data.

I first thought to estimate the model for pathological data, then try to
process data to make it look healthy and then using the pathological
estimate as a prior, do model comparison on which intervention matches
pseudo-healthy data best.

Is this remotely reasonable? Are there standard methods / formulations
for this sort of problem amenable to Stan's inference algorithms?

(sorry for the rather generic question)

Thank you,
Marmaduke

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] comparing intervention models
parts:
No, I don't think what you suggest is reasaonble.

Yes, there are standard methods for this kind of
thing. Yes, they are amenable to Stan's inference.

I'd suggest this:

http://arxiv.org/abs/1507.04544

but you'll probably have to do some background reading first.

- Bob
